subject: Copywriting
title: Classified Ads and the Want Ad
description: A quick, practical guide to Classified Ads and the Want Ad.

hook.text: Classified ads charged by the word. Every letter cost money. This forced writers to be ruthlessly concise.

buildup.text: Abbreviations bloomed: 'rm' for room, 'nr' for near, 'gd cond' for good condition. Brevity was survival.

discovery.text: The constraint created a craft. The best classified writers packed maximum meaning into minimum words.

twist.text: Craigslist killed paid classifieds by making them free. Newspapers lost billions in revenue.

climax.text: Twitter's 140-character limit echoed classifieds. Paying per word and paying per character breed the same skill.

punchline.text: Pay per word, write per word. Constraints make better copy.

quiz.question: Why were classified ads so concise?
options: Advertisers were charged by the word

details.summary: Classified advertising organized commercial messages by category — jobs, real estate, personals, goods for sale — creating a searchable marketplace within newspapers. For over 200 years, classifieds were the backbone of newspaper revenue. Their decline with Craigslist and online marketplaces...
details.whyItMatters: Classifieds demonstrate how a simple organizational format can create enormous economic value — and how digital disruption can destroy it overnight. They are the origin story of online marketplaces.
takeaways: Classified ads organized commercial messages by category for easy search
They were the primary revenue source for newspapers for over two centuries
Craigslist and online marketplaces destroyed the classified ad business model

faq.question: How did Craigslist destroy newspaper classifieds?
faq.answer: Craigslist offered free classified listings online, eliminating the scarcity that newspapers relied on. Between 2000 and 2012, newspaper classified revenue dropped from $19.6 billion to $4.6 billion. This single change was a primary cause of the newspaper industry's financial crisis.

faq.question: What made classified ads work for so long?
faq.answer: They solved a matching problem: connecting buyers with sellers efficiently. The categorical organization made them searchable. Their newspaper placement reached a broad local audience. This utility made them indispensable until the internet offered a better solution.
